o1.biggest_strength: It correctly targets the high-churn Essentials 8+ segment with a flat Agency plan and names Team cannibalization as the key risk.
o1.biggest_mistake: It wrongly downplays the yearly-billing opportunity even though the data shows it is under-used and materially lowers churn, and its revenue table is not fully transparent enough to trust without rework.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add the honest yearly push into the recommendation and show the scenario math step by step, with the first test focused on the existing at-risk 8+ segment as well as new visitors.

o2.biggest_strength: It focuses on the exact leaking segment, uses the churn and revenue data cleanly, and gives a concrete flat-plan test with clear pass and stop rules.
o2.biggest_mistake: It mentions yearly billing only at the Agency switch instead of making the broader under-used annual-billing push a more explicit part of the pricing change.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the yearly-billing nudge explicit on the pricing page and in-app after signup, while keeping the Agency plan as the main pricing move.

reason: Output 2 is the one I could take to the team: the math is easier to audit, the test is aimed at the existing churn problem, and the customer message fits the brand. Output 1 has the right core idea, but it misses the yearly-billing signal and makes the revenue case less convincingly.
